prompt: An ambulance with its siren on drives past a stationary listener. Describe what the listener hears and explain why.
markscheme: Higher pitch as it approaches and lower pitch as it moves away **(A1)**; the source's motion compresses the wavefronts ahead of it (shorter wavelength, higher observed frequency) and stretches them behind **(R1)**

concept: Wavefront diagrams for a moving source
prompt: A source moves to the right while emitting waves. On a wavefront diagram, the wavefronts are:
options: concentric circles centred on the source
markscheme: **C.** Each wavefront is a circle centred on where the source **was** when it was emitted, so the circles crowd together on the right (ahead) and spread out on the left.

prompt: A hydrogen line emitted at 656.3 nm is observed at 662.9 nm in the spectrum of a galaxy. Calculate the galaxy's velocity relative to the Earth.
The spectral lines from one edge of a rotating galaxy are redshifted and those from the opposite edge are blueshifted, relative to the centre. Explain what this shows.
markscheme: Redshift: that edge is moving away from us; blueshift: the other edge is moving towards us **(R1)**; so the galaxy is rotating, and the size of the shifts gives its rotational speed (used to infer its mass) **(R1)**

prompt:
A siren emits 800 Hz. The speed of sound is $340\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.

**(a)** Calculate the frequency heard by a stationary observer as the siren approaches at $25\ \text{m s}^{-1}$, and as it moves away at the same speed. **[2]**

**(b)** Calculate the frequency heard by an observer moving at $25\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ towards a stationary siren, and comment on the comparison with (a). **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** Approaching: $f'=800\times\dfrac{340}{340-25}=864$ Hz **(A1)**; receding: $800\times\dfrac{340}{340+25}=745$ Hz **(A1)**

**(b)** $f'=800\times\dfrac{340+25}{340}=859$ Hz **(A1)**; different from 864 Hz: for sound the result depends on whether the source or the observer moves relative to the medium **(R1)**
